text:
sam_support: Heads-up — acme-pay is seeing sustained 429s across a subset of their endpoints since ~03:10 UTC. They say it looks like minute-aligned bursts but their client claims steady request rate. CX attached a snippet of their client logs and our gateway responses. Can someone triage?

priya_sre: On it. Can you paste one full request/response (headers + status) and the x-rate-limit headers if present? Also need region and model route they hit.

sam_support: Pasting sample from the gateway edge logs:

```
[2026-08-07T03:12:21Z] INFO request_id=abc123 client=acme-pay route=/v1/generate status=429 x-rate-limit-limit=600 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=12
[2026-08-07T03:12:22Z] INFO request_id=abc124 client=acme-pay route=/v1/generate status=429 x-rate-limit-limit=600 x-rate-limit-remaining=0 x-rate-limit-reset=11
```

Customer also sent this quick repro curl they run every 200ms from a single container: 

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "rwd-small-v1", "prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 64}'
```

They say they maintained the same cadence for weeks, this started today. They shared their rate-limit headers which match the log above.

miguel_runtime: Few notes: 600 RPM ~= 10 RPS sustained per API key. If they're firing every 200ms from one container that's 5 RPS from that single process, but the customer might have multiple replicas or SDK retries inflating it. Also watch TPM — short prompts with low token counts can still hit RPM if concurrency high.

priya_sre: Check whether their requests are multiplexed (HTTP/2) or multiple TCP connections. If they're opening new connections each minute, token/time bucketing can create minute-boundary spikes. Can we get a quick metrics snapshot? sam, can you pull the per-minute traffic graph (edge/gateway) for api_key=acme-pay for the last 60m?

sam_support: Pulling now... attaching top-level numbers: peak RPM observed 820 at 03:12, average 420 last hour. TPM was 19k at peak. They are on Hosted US-EAST, model pinned to rwd-small-v1.

miguel_runtime: 820 RPM > configured limit 600 -> 429 expected. But we should verify whether backpressure is applied evenly or bucketed by route/customer. If the customer is bursting at minute boundaries, the client-side 200ms loop could be synchronized with some cron elsewhere, causing spikes. Ask customer for number of containers and whether they have a retry loop.

priya_sre: Also check gateway logs for token bucket refill granularity. We had a change earlier this month that tightened per-minute windows for some front-proxies; if their traffic aligns, they can see sudden 429s even though smoothed RPS seems low.

sam_support: Replied to customer asking for: # of replicas, whether they use SDK (which may auto-retry), and a timed trace of requests per second. Also suggested they back off with exponential jitter. They asked if we can increase their RPM temporarily while they debug.

miguel_runtime: We can do a temporary quota bump on Hosted for debugging but prefer to validate client behavior first. If they need surge capacity, offer a short Dedicated burst or suggest enabling our burst-bucket feature (if eligible). For immediate triage: collect a pcap or full request timestamps, and try an authenticated replay from a controlled runner to reproduce.

priya_sre: Quick commands for logs/diagnostics: 

```
# gateway recent errors
kubectl logs -l app=gateway -c gateway --since=15m | grep acme-pay | tail -n 200

# edge-batcher debug
kubectl logs -l app=edge-batcher -c batcher --since=30m | grep "request_id=abc"

# metrics
promql: sum(rate(http_requests_total{api_key="acme-pay"}[1m])) by (instance)
```

sam_support: Ran the prometheus query — shows two containers with short synchronized pulses at top-of-minute causing spikes. Customer confirmed they have a cron that flushes a small backlog every minute (they thought 1/min was fine).

miguel_runtime: That explains it. A concentrated minute-aligned flush from multiple containers will blow past RPM buckets. Recommend they spread retries with jitter or use a token-bucket client-side. We should also offer them guidance doc and an example backoff snippet: 

```
# very lightweight jittered backoff
for attempt in range(n):
  sleep((base_backoff * 2**attempt) * random.uniform(0.75, 1.25))
```

priya_sre: Action items:
- sam: offer a temporary +30% RPM bump for 2 hours to allow replay tests (needs approvals)
- miguel: add a short KB on minute-boundary spikes and include a recommended client jitter snippet in SDK docs
- sam: collect post-replay metrics and close loop with customer

sam_support: Filed internal approval for a 2-hour bump, ETA 20m. I told the customer to stagger their cron and try again; they will run a controlled replay from a single host.

ops-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-0472 — acme-pay 429 spike, temp quota bump requested.

priya_sre: If the customer still sees > limit after jittering and spreading, we'll need a deeper look into whether gateway mis-attribution or duplicated requests are occurring (proxies re-sending). For now this reads like classic minute-batch burst.

sam_support: Customer did a controlled replay from one host and peak dropped to 580 RPM, no 429s in 15m. They will roll the fix to prod with jitter. Closing unless anything else.

miguel_runtime: Great. Later we should consider adding a small guidance pop-up in Console when customers hit sustained 429s about client-side jitter and the difference between RPM/TPM.

sam_support: Closing thread. Will follow up if they come back after rollout. :white_check_mark:
